requirements.requirement: Rotate /var/log/inventory/app.log daily and keep seven compressed rotations
requirements.summary: Config /etc/logrotate.d/inventory-app specifies daily, rotate 7, compress, delaycompress, missingok, notifempty, copytruncate, create 0644 root root. logrotate -d validated syntax with no errors. Two forced rotation cycles produced app.log.1 (plain, delaycompress-held) then app.log.2.gz (compressed on the following cycle), demonstrating the delaycompress+compress+rotate pipeline functions as configured. system logrotate.timer (daily trigger) is active and enabled both pre- and post-restart, and the config file was confirmed still present after reboot. Only 3 of the 7 retained slots were exercised (app.log.1/.2.gz/.3.gz), which is expected since fully exhausting a 7-day retention window is not practical to force live, but the rotate 7 directive itself is directly present and read by logrotate.

requirements.requirement: Allow the application to continue writing to app.log after rotation
requirements.summary: copytruncate was chosen (no process holds the file open per lsof check), guaranteeing the log path stays in place across rotation. After each forced rotation, new lines ('post-rotation line', 'post-reboot write after rotation') were successfully appended to app.log and confirmed via cat, both before and after the node restart.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on node1: pre-restart healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered state
requirements.summary: Pre-restart baseline (cmd-8aa48e0eacdc4cbd) captured boot_id e8afb731..., config, log dir state, and timer status. Reboot was acknowledged and dispatched (cmd-0a01bdd5eb1a4f87), followed by an observed connection timeout confirming disconnection (cmd-ac6c05988102467c). Post-restart polling showed a new boot_id cb593cfa... (cmd-56fce067a7ed4fb0), matching the fixed after_executor boot-identity snapshot. Recovery verification (cmd-6845eb4ea2404046) confirmed the logrotate config persisted, the timer remained active/enabled, and a fresh forced rotation plus write succeeded, demonstrating full functional recovery of the configured rotation behavior after reboot.

overall_summary: The executor configured /etc/logrotate.d/inventory-app with daily/rotate 7/compress/delaycompress/copytruncate, validated the syntax, and directly demonstrated working rotation and continued writability across two forced rotation cycles both before and after a full node reboot with a verified changed boot identity. All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct evidence, and the mandatory node-restart protocol was completed cleanly with no unnecessary mutations or residue.
limitations: Only 3 of the 7 configured retained rotations were actually produced during the observation window, so full 7-slot retention behavior over multiple real days was not directly exercised (though the rotate 7 directive is present and read without error).

No original application writer process was observed (lsof showed nothing holding app.log open), so copytruncate's benefit versus an active writer was inferred rather than observed against a live process producing continuous log output.

operational_hygiene.summary: All 8 executor commands have a clear purpose: two are read-only discovery/inspection (cmd-48ce0161be9c4a4c, cmd-ce5833190e1040c3), one writes and validates the logrotate config plus exercises two forced rotation cycles to prove the setup works (cmd-f2902665c2964f7e), one captures the mandatory pre-restart baseline (cmd-8aa48e0eacdc4cbd), the reboot and its acknowledgement/timeout pair are the mandatory restart action (cmd-0a01bdd5eb1a4f87, cmd-ac6c05988102467c), one confirms the new boot identity (cmd-56fce067a7ed4fb0), and the final command performs mandatory post-restart recovery verification (cmd-6845eb4ea2404046). No unnecessary or unreverted mutations were found: the only state changes are the intended logrotate config file, the intentionally forced log rotations (an expected artifact of validating the rotation scheme), and the reboot itself. Failed-services and package-health checks are clean and unchanged in both fixed snapshots; listening-socket and /tmp differences are attributable solely to the reboot (new boot-id-scoped systemd-private dirs, refreshed PIDs) and are not executor residue.
